key_insight: Strategically organizing training data—by reusing pre-computed sample-level scores to control order, grouping, and scheduling—can significantly improve LLM training efficiency and outcomes when models are trained for only one or a few epochs.
problem_solved: Addresses the underexplored challenge of how to organize (order, group, and schedule) training data to maximize learning from limited-pass LLM training, beyond the widely studied problem of data selection.
method: Reuse pre-computed sample-level scores (e.g., quality/difficulty) as signals to drive data ordering and batching during training.
Compare organization strategies (curriculum, anti-curriculum, stratified/clustered batches, prioritized replay) across one/few-epoch regimes to isolate their effects.
Perform systematic ablations and controlled training runs to quantify impacts on convergence speed and generalization.
impact: Enables practitioners to extract more signal from the same data and compute budget by optimizing how data is presented to the model, improving sample efficiency and making short-run LLM training more predictable and effective.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: pre-computed scoring → organization strategy (order/batch) → training loop
Line chart: validation loss or accuracy over steps comparing random order vs organized strategies
Bar chart: relative sample-efficiency or final metric gains for different organization methods
Illustration of batch construction (curriculum vs stratified vs prioritized) to show practical implementation
paper_title: Demystifying Data Organization for Enhanced LLM Training
paper_authors: Yalun Dai, Yangyu Huang, Tongshen Yang, Yonghan Wang, Xin Zhang
